title: Targeted purity sentinels around classifier-reachable I/O surfaces — NOT class-level `Path.stat` monkeypatch
body:
The current `test_classifier_is_pure_no_io` patches `Path.stat` at the class level via `monkeypatch.setattr(Path, 'stat', _explode)` to assert the classifier touches no disk. Two failure modes intertwined:

(a) When the underlying assertion fails for any reason, pytest's traceback formatter (`_pytest/_code/code.py`) calls `code.path` which calls `p.exists()` which calls `self.stat()` — still patched as `_explode` — turning a normal test red into `INTERNALERROR`. This makes the test fragile to any unrelated assertion failure under it.

(b) Pytest's framework internals + capture machinery + numerous innocuous third-party libraries call `Path.stat` and `Path.exists` benignly during test setup/teardown. Trapping them at the class level catches all those.

Locked patch set:

- `subprocess.run` (the classifier's only legitimate I/O candidate, via the now-removed `resolve_repo` call — see D002)
- `Path.read_text`
- `Path.write_text`
- `Path.open`

Explicitly NOT patched: `Path.stat`, `Path.exists`. They're framework-load-bearing.

Reason: each sentinel surface is a *write or read of file content* a pure classifier should never do. `stat`/`exists` are existence/metadata probes the framework itself uses; trapping them produces false positives (framework internals) and false negatives (classifier could call `Path.stat()` without reading content; but the classifier doesn't — and if it ever did, content sentinels would still trip when the classifier read the result).

How to apply: F001 step 5 codifies the patch set. F001 acceptance #1-#3 lock the no-INTERNALERROR property + the explicit grep assertion that `Path.stat` and `Path.exists` are NOT in the patch set.

title: Classifier-local pure repo derivation — NOT `resolve_repo()` modification
body:
Two reject options:

(a) Modify `target_context_prelude.resolve_repo()` to accept a pre-resolved repo argument that the classifier passes. Rejected because the classifier *should not have any filesystem seam at all* — adding an argument acknowledges the seam exists.

(b) Inject a `stat_fn` (or other I/O dependency) into the classifier as a parameter. Same rejection — the classifier shouldn't need any I/O dependency.

Locked approach: `classify_ec5_severity()` stops calling `resolve_repo()` entirely. It picks `repo` for the canonical render comparison purely from envelope data:

```python
def _derive_classifier_repo(tc, parsed):
    if tc and tc.get('repo'):
        return tc['repo']
    if parsed is not None and 'repo' in parsed:
        return parsed['repo']
    return None
```

Semantics:

- If `target_context.repo` is present and truthy → use it (the standard structured-target path).
- Else if a prelude was parsed and contains a `repo` field → use that (preserves historical `Repo: Jarvis` fixtures predating the DontPanic rename — see D005).
- Else → None; the existing missing-prelude i0 / struct-incomplete i1 semantics keep applying.

`resolve_repo()` itself stays in `target_context_prelude.py` byte-identical (greppable assertion). Other callers (notably `audit_writer._normalize_summary` for prelude injection) continue to use it as today.

Reason: the classifier's job is to compare an envelope's stated target against the parsed prelude's claims. Both are present in the envelope itself — there's no need to reach out to git or the filesystem. The historical `resolve_repo` call was always over-reach; Plan D removes it cleanly without adding new seams.

How to apply: F001 step 2 + acceptance #4-#6 lock the implementation + grep assertions.

title: Historical fixtures with `Repo: Jarvis` remain valid post-DontPanic-rename
body:
Test fixtures predating the canonical-module-rename (Plan A) carry `Repo: Jarvis` in their prelude blocks. After Plan A merged, the cwd-resolved repo basename is `DontPanic` — a string mismatch that classified those fixtures as i1 (value-mismatch) instead of `none` (golden).

The operator-added AC (acceptance item #7): `test_case_c_golden_returns_none` must pass WITHOUT cwd repo fallback. Specifically: when `target_context.repo` is absent and the summary has a parseable prelude with `Repo: Jarvis`, the classifier must return `'none'` — proving the classifier-local repo derivation correctly uses the parsed prelude's value as the comparison reference.

This is a direct test of D002's correctness: the classifier compares the envelope's parsed prelude against itself (using the same `repo` value from the prelude as both the canonical render input AND the comparison target), so any prelude-internal consistency holds regardless of what the cwd-resolved repo string would be.

Reason: historical fixtures are durable test data. Plan D's purity fix must not invalidate them. The reference value for the classifier's render comparison is the envelope's own prelude, not the filesystem.

How to apply: F001 acceptance #7 explicitly asserts `test_case_c_golden_returns_none` passes for the historical-fixture scenario. The fixture files themselves are NOT modified.

title: F001 close-out — EC5 classifier purity caveat closed; full suite green without --ignore
body:
F001 shipped via direct path. Two-part fix landed in two files:

1. `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/ec5_classifier.py` — replaced `resolve_repo(tc)` call with new `_derive_classifier_repo(tc, parsed)` helper (pure function, no filesystem reach). Removed `resolve_repo` from the `target_context_prelude` import. The classifier now picks `repo` from envelope data only: `tc.get('repo')` first, else `parsed['repo']` (preserves historical `Repo: Jarvis` fixtures per D005), else None.

2. `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/tests/test_ec5_classifier.py` — replaced `monkeypatch.setattr(Path, 'stat', _explode)` with the locked targeted sentinel set per D001: `subprocess.run`, `Path.read_text`, `Path.write_text`, `Path.open`. Path.stat and Path.exists explicitly NOT patched. Added `import subprocess`. Renamed `_explode` → `_trip` to match D001's wording.

Verification:

- Targeted ec5_classifier: 20 passed in 0.17s. Both `test_classifier_is_pure_no_io` (AC #1, #3) and `test_case_c_golden_returns_none` (AC #7) pass cleanly.

- INTERNALERROR-gone proof: deliberately injecting an `assert False` under the targeted sentinels produces a normal `AssertionError`, not `INTERNALERROR`. Pytest's traceback formatter no longer hits a class-level `Path.stat` trap.
- Ruff check + format clean across touched files.

EC5-specific Q: classifier responsibility stays at the platform boundary; verified at code level (`ec5_classifier.py:99` calls pure `_derive_classifier_repo()` at line 114 reading envelope-only data, no subprocess.run, no filesystem reach), test-sentinel level (lines 295-298 patch only classifier-reachable I/O — `subprocess.run` + `Path.read_text/write_text/open`; `Path.stat`/`Path.exists` deliberately excluded per D001 to avoid pytest formatter `INTERNALERROR`), and protected-path level (`target_context_prelude.py` byte-identical pre/post per D002 + protected_paths declaration; `resolve_repo()` itself unchanged, still subprocess-using, still consumed by `audit_writer._normalize_summary` and other callers).

(4) Plan-level memo: existing impl-time content NOT modified. Appended single new section `Status-flip close-out verification (added 2026-05-07)` recording: (i) the platform/agent-boundary MAY/MUST-NOT table per operator framing — classifier MAY classify structural target-context conditions and prose-vs-structured prelude form, MUST NOT subprocess for env inference / infer agent intent / judge auditor reasoning quality / classify prompt-format variance; (ii) Phase B caveat citation resolves cleanly under the narrow naming (`F001/D011 — EC5 classifier purity regression in test_ec5_classifier.py`), not under any broader 'EC5 / prompt-format issues' framing; (iii) explicit non-subsumption list — auditor-prompt quality, `resolve_repo()` itself, other queued caveats, broader content-correctness/semantic-truth judgment all remain separate concerns.

(5) D010 appended without reconstructing D001-D009. (6) `dontpanic plan close` exempt-flow path. (7) Re-validate clean. (8) Commit scoped to plan dir.

Phase B caveat citation — fairly markable closed: Phase B's plan-closeout-memo cites this plan as `F001/D011 — EC5 classifier purity regression in test_ec5_classifier.py`. That's the narrow naming. This plan addresses both root causes of that specific regression (cwd-dependent `resolve_repo()` mismatching historical `Repo: Jarvis` fixtures + class-level `Path.stat` monkeypatch turning assertion failures into `INTERNALERROR`). The full orchestrate sweep now runs without the `--ignore=test_ec5_classifier.py` exclusion that threaded through Plans A/B/C close-outs.
